title.narrative: Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Country Programme

description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's DRC Country Programme works to unlock the trade potential of Africa's second-largest country by tackling the structural bottlenecks that constrain both formal and informal trade, particularly in Eastern DRC. Operating along the Northern, Central, Lobito, and Kribi-Zongo corridors, the Programme invests in physical trade infrastructure, including One Stop Border Post upgrades at Mahagi and Ruzizi II and port modernisation at Kalundu and Kasenyi on Lake Tanganyika, while advancing digital customs systems such as ASYCUDA World and the Single Electronic Window (SEGUCE) to cut clearance times and reduce opportunities for corruption. Complementing these hard and digital infrastructure interventions, the Programme supports alignment of DRC's trade policy with AfCFTA and EAC protocols, strengthens quality standards and sanitary and phytosanitary systems, and runs targeted initiatives, including the Women in Trade Programme to transition informal traders, particularly women in Goma and Bukavu, into formal trade channels and connect them to regional markets.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.
